conviction_note: A near-non-result. Every sourced fact either sits inside the company's July guide (Fed hike assumed, NIM drifting down a couple of bps a quarter, period-end share count already public) or is small against a ~$1.21 EPS bar: a softer mortgage line from the MBA series, and provision risk shown in the company's own September deck (Moody's unemployment path 4.5% to 5.0%, NPLs up to 1.17% on three credits). The stock rose 3.2% the session after the Q2 NPL jump, so credit worry has not been punished. abs_move 3.0 sits above the name's 2.3% median reaction because the options are unusable, the print moves to bmo with a same-morning call, and the core says to size up; p_up 49 is a coin flip with a hair of negative lean. The findings sum to -0.3 and the scaled number is -0.06. Both are near zero and agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $1.21. Two sources agree: Benzinga's forecast table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/fbk/earnings-forecasts, Oct 1 snapshot) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/FBK). Revenue consensus is about $179.7m to $181.2m. My arithmetic: Q2 adjusted NI $58.9m over roughly 50.0m period-end shares is about $1.18, plus a normalised provision gets to about $1.21 to $1.24, while a Q2-like $10m provision puts it near $1.16 to $1.18. So my central read is in line, and the swing factor is the provision. Company guide (Q2 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504): FY NIM excluding accretion 3.70% to 3.80%, loans up mid-to-high single digits, banking-segment expense $325m to $335m, efficiency ratio around 50%.
positioning_check: Short interest is 3,045,421 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 6.1% of shares outstanding and 3.75 days to cover (equibles.com/stocks/fbk/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12, via the sweep row). That is moderate, not crowded. Skew is null and the chain is unusable: total open interest 33, ATM spread 66% of mid. So the 11.9% implied move is not a market price and there is no directional statement from options. Run-up is -3.03% over 20 days and +1.73% over 5 days; the stock is 13.8% below its 52-week high and 5% above its low.

findings.finding: Mortgage demand weakened through Q3. The MBA purchase index was 157.5 in the week reported 2026-09-10, down from 169.7 in late May, and the 30-year rate reached a ~14-month high of 6.85%. FBK's mortgage banking income, already down to $11.2m in Q2 from $12.3m in Q1, is likely lower again, perhaps $1m to $2m pre-tax, which is about $0.02 to $0.03 of EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mortgage income fell $1.1m in Q2 (company attributed it to retaining loans on balance sheet), and the stock rose 3.23% the next session. There is no evidence that this line moves the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of about $180m to $181m is above Q2's roughly $175m adjusted. If the street had marked mortgage fees down, the revenue bar would sit nearer Q2's level. The effect is small (mortgage is about 6% of revenue), so it may simply not have been modelled.
findings.independence: Proxy only: industry series to company transmission, not confirmed by FBK. The company's own Q2 release shows the line already declining (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm). Net of the rest: NII is about 85% of revenue and was guided to grow with loans, so this finding is a small drag at most.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% on 2026-09-16. FBK's July outlook explicitly assumed one Q3 hike, and the company says it is asset-sensitive (a couple of million dollars of benefit from higher rates), so the rate path came in as the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM has been stable, at 3.94% to 3.95% across Q1 and Q2 2026. The stock's reactions over the last seven prints are -4.6% to +4.1% with no NIM-driven outlier identifiable.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the hike was forecast and it matches the company's own assumption. Only about two weeks of the hike fall inside Q3. Any edge is in whether the FY NIM guide is held or firmed, which would show as a tightened range on the call. Nothing visible suggests the street expects a change.
findings.independence: The company's rate assumption is in the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504). Cutting the other way, management also said deposit and loan pricing competition would offset part of the benefit, and that caveat is netted into the small size.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21 FBK priced $125m of 6.625% fixed-to-floating subordinated notes due 2036. The stated use is capital to FirstBank to support growth. Total capital goes from 12.9% to 13.7% pro forma, CET1 is unchanged at 11.0%, and existing debt has call dates from 2026-12-31.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior debt raise sits inside the baseline's reaction window.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small: about $2m a quarter of pre-tax interest if it is not used to refinance, and roughly 0 in Q3. The question is what it buys. The demand is corroborated: Q2 loans grew 11.6% annualised, the pipeline was 'just as big', and CET1 fell to 11.0% after a 3% buyback. So it funds growth and capital rebuilding, and is not a distress signal. Signed zero after that answer.
findings.independence: Use of proceeds and the capital table come from the 424B5. Loan growth and pipeline come from the Q2 release and call (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504). The call dates are from the fixed-income deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1649749/000121390026100750/ea030565201ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Period-end shares were 49.98m against roughly 51.9m Q2 diluted average ($58.6m / $1.13). Most of the 1.55m Q2 buyback came in June, so the Q3 average share count is about 3.5% lower, which mechanically adds about $0.04 to EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated reaction to share count.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The period-end count is in the release, and the $1.21 consensus (up from $1.14) likely already includes it. The finding is kept small for that reason. If the street had not modelled it, consensus would sit near $1.17.
findings.independence: The 10-Q repurchase table confirms the buyback was weighted to June at an average of $54.44 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000060/fbk-20260630.htm). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Provision is the swing on the EPS bar. NPLs rose to 1.17% from 0.96% in Q2 on three relationships, and Q2 provision was $10.1m against $3.0m in Q1. The company's own September deck carries Moody's June path for its CECL inputs: unemployment 4.5% in 3Q26, rising to 5.0%, and house prices down 2.9% in 4Q26. Since then the Fed has hiked, and 16% of office loans mature by year-end 2026. A second ~$10m provision would put EPS near $1.16 to $1.18, below the $1.21 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print carried the NPL jump and a $10.1m provision, and the stock rose 3.23% the next session. The market looked through credit last time.
findings.why_not_priced: A $1.21 consensus that rises $0.07 off Q2 is roughly what normalising provision plus share count produce. That bar has no room for a repeat reserve build. If the street had priced credit risk, Q3 estimates would sit nearer $1.15 to $1.17. Against that, the stock is already 13.8% off its high and down 3% over 20 days.
findings.independence: The NPL and provision figures come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm), which the deck restates. The rate hike is the forexfundamentals FOMC page. Management called the three credits borrower-specific and said NCOs were 6bp. That is a caveat, not a contradiction, and it is why the size is small. No 2026 press coverage of a new FirstBank problem credit was found.

outside_window.finding: From Q4 the $125m of 6.625% sub notes adds about $2m a quarter of interest expense unless it refinances debt callable from 2026-12-31. It matters for Q4 NII and the debt-call decision, not for this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Peer Q3 2026 prints from US regional or Southeast banks before 2026-10-12: none found. The only Q3 2026 bank results found were Canadian fiscal quarters ending July 31.
H.8 small-bank loan and deposit data for Q3 2026: FRED pages found were stale (latest deposit points Feb-Mar 2026).
FirstBank litigation, foreclosure, developer bankruptcy or layoff news in 2026: nothing beyond old cases.
Q3 buyback disclosure (no 8-K) and post-June-30 data in the two September 2026 decks and the 424B5: none. All data is as of 2026-06-30, and there is no Recent Developments section.
Q2 10-Q credit-quality footnotes, subsequent events and rate sensitivity: the fetch returned only the front portion, so this was not readable.
Form 4s dated 2026-10-01 (three filings on 10-08): not opened. They are likely routine quarterly director grants, and nothing indicates open-market activity.
The July reaction conflict (Chartmill after-hours -12.4% versus the baseline's +3.23% next-session move) was not resolved. The baseline's exact 8-K-timed figure was used.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild negative lean (provision, mortgage) runs with the soft 20-day run-up and the 13.8% drawdown from the high, so it is partly priced. The name's last reaction to an NPL jump was +3.2%, which argues for a small size.
lessons_applied: Rule 4 (financing is a question): the sub-debt raise went from -0.1 to 0.0. The use of proceeds is growth and capital, corroborated by 11.6% annualised loan growth and an intact pipeline.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Fed-hike finding went from +0.2 to +0.1, because the July guide already assumed the hike.
Rule 1 (reaction history): the credit/provision finding went from -0.4 to -0.3. The stock rose 3.23% after the Q2 NPL jump.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the mortgage proxy went from -0.3 to -0.2. Mortgage is about 6% of revenue, and NII was guided to grow.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': p_up moved from 48 to 49.
Left standing: the share-count finding at +0.1, the $1.21 bar (two agreeing sources, so no cap), and abs_move_pct at 3.0.
